Re-add under the same data_id looks up Data globally, updates owner/content in place and resets pipeline_status but leaves old graph/vector derivatives. A caller-supplied id must therefore include physical user and active-tenant scope, and replacement must purge derivatives first.
Data.id is the relational table's global primary key; owner_id and tenant_id do not participate in uniqueness. Both are required inputs to caller-derived data_id values.

User.id is the canonical owner id and nullable User.tenant_id is the mutable active-tenant selector; both form LocalCogneeRuntime's physical identity scope.
Returns a full default User. LocalCogneeRuntime resolves it for every operation instead of caching only its id, so default-user or active-tenant drift is detected.
Refreshes one explicit User including active tenant. LocalCogneeRuntime compares the refreshed user-and-tenant coordinates with its configured snapshot before SDK mutation.
Dataset ownership has separate owner_id and tenant_id columns; name alone or name plus owner is not a complete physical lookup key.

Permission-based dataset listing filters results to the supplied User's active tenant; shared datasets can still share a name, so LocalCogneeRuntime additionally requires owner_id.

Per-dataset graph/vector context accepts user_id and re-fetches the User to select tenant-specific storage. Active tenant must not change concurrently; connector validation can detect drift only before the upstream re-read.
